meta.title: DIP overall workflow

system.name: DIP
system.one_liner: a dynamic, modality-aware pipeline scheduling framework for large multimodal model training

meta.caption_draft: The overall workflow of DIP. Before training, the LMM model is partitioned into model chunks by the model chunk partitioner. During each training iteration, DIP asynchronously executes a four-stage online planning process: (1) prefetch batch metadata, (2) split microbatches into modality-specific sub-microbatches, (3) search candidate pipeline schedules, (4) deploy the chosen schedule to the GPU training workers.
open_questions: The offline phase runs once and the online phase runs per iteration -- should the two dashed groups be labelled with their cadence ('once' / 'per iteration')?
The shared simulator is used by two components; is 'uses' the right word, or does the paper call it a query?
meta._notes: Captured: the two dashed phase groups, the four circled steps on the online loop only, the self-loop on the schedule searcher, the dotted 'uses' links to the shared simulator, and the fact that the batch/worker row sits BETWEEN the two dashed boxes (the source SVG's dashed rects span y 0-51 and y 99-177 of 178, so neither encloses that row -- semantics.json puts 'Training batches' inside Online Planner, which the drawing does not). Not captured: the three raster icons (LMM cube, batch thumbnail strip, GPU chip) are recorded as kind=icon plus a symbol description; the drawer substitutes a vector symbol or draws its own. The four pastel tints inside the model-chunk stack (one per destination GPU) collapse into multiplicity + a note.
